findings.description: D6 and tasks 3.8a/5.6 have converge() build a second, tool-less packet and 'pass both paths to dispatch_and_wait', and have dispatch_and_wait hand the tool-less body and its tools_overflow flag to OpenAI-compatible adapters. That needs a new optional dispatch_and_wait parameter (for both ReviewOrchestrator and the CompositeOrchestrator that converge() calls through _accepts_kwarg) and a new tools_overflow keyword on OpenAICompatAdapter.dispatch. Neither is named anywhere, and the cross-cutting interface contract table lists only include_lanes for dispatch_and_wait. Groups 3 and 5 implement the two sides of this interface in separate packages.
findings.resolution: Name the parameter (for example toolless_packet_path: Path | None = None) in D6, and add rows to the interface contract table for it and for OpenAICompatAdapter.dispatch(tools_overflow=False), both additive with defaults that keep current behaviour.

findings.description: The Metered Review Lane Spend Accounting requirement says every review an openrouter lane dispatches is recorded with spend_recorder.record(), and acceptance outcome 3 says every OpenRouter review is recorded against the ceiling. The only task that calls record() is 5.5, inside agent_lane's CompositeOrchestrator. D5 also selects the metered lane on a host with fewer than fill_target non-metered lanes (for example one CLI vendor and OPENROUTER_API_KEY in non-OpenBao mode). That review runs through ReviewOrchestrator.dispatch_and_wait from converge() or /parallel-review-*, never through agent_lane, so its spend is neither recorded nor spooled and no metered_spend_unrecorded degradation is raised.
findings.resolution: Move the record() call to the dispatcher: ReviewOrchestrator.dispatch_and_wait calls spend_recorder.record() after each OpenAI-compatible result and marks the ReviewResult (for example spend_recorded: bool) so callers can raise metered_spend_unrecorded. CompositeOrchestrator then gets this for free. Update task 5.5, the group that owns the change (group 3 then depends on group 4), and the dependency graph.

findings.description: The spec fixes work_unit_ref as '<change_id>:<review_type>:round-<n>'. IMPL_REVIEW and VAL_REVIEW both run with review_type 'implementation', so their rows get the same work_unit_ref and spend cannot be split by phase. This is the collision the round-2 fix already removed for the consensus files. Design D4 allows '<phase|review_type>'.
findings.resolution: Use the phase in the spec: work_unit_ref = '<change_id>:<phase>:round-<n>' (for example 'openrouter-review-lane:VAL_REVIEW:round-2').

findings.description: D4 and task 5.7 put the per-round budget re-check in converge(). converge() is vendor-agnostic: it receives only verified_lanes and an orchestrator, does not know which lanes are metered, has no coordinator-usage client, and has no way to keep one lane out of a dispatch except through orchestrator-specific kwargs. CompositeOrchestrator already knows the metered lanes and builds include_lanes, so the check fits there, or in ReviewOrchestrator.dispatch_and_wait next to the probe code. Keeping it in converge() widens the converge() signature with routing concerns.
findings.resolution: Run the re-check in the dispatch layer (CompositeOrchestrator, or dispatch_and_wait for metered lanes), which returns the synthetic vendor_unavailable/spend_ceiling_exceeded ReviewResult. converge() then only applies the D7 mapping. Change D4 and task 5.7 to match.
